idiom_name: sealed interface + record cases + exhaustive pattern switch
implementation_notes: Java 17 sealing (JEP 409) declares the complete set (sealed interface Shape permits Circle, Rect, Triangle {}, with permits inferred when the cases share the compilation unit), records carry the payloads, and Java 21 pattern matching for switch (JEP 441) checks type coverage against the permits clause, so a switch expression with one arm per case and no default is exhaustive by compiler rule. That is the exact replacement for a Visitor: the element types keep no accept() method and each operation is one switch in the class that needs it. The proof is compile-time only and migration-sensitive - a sealed hierarchy that gains a permitted subclass and is recompiled without its switch sites makes those switches throw MatchException - so the hierarchy and its matches must be built together.
pitfalls: A default arm switches off the coverage proof: javac accepts one happily, and every future variant then lands in it silently.
Adding a permitted subclass without recompiling the switch sites throws MatchException at run time (JEP 441), so exhaustive switches must be rebuilt with the sealed hierarchy.
Exhaustiveness needs a sealed or enum selector: over an ordinary interface the default arm is mandatory and the guarantee is gone.
Sealed hierarchies must stay inside one module or package (unnamed module); a permitted subclass in another module does not compile.

variants.name: Enum class as the closed set with an exhaustive switch expression (Java 14+)
variants.implementation_notes: Before sealed types the Java shape of the pattern is an enum: the constant set is closed by the language, switch expressions (Java 14) over an enum selector are rejected by javac when a constant is missing and no default is present, and shared per-variant data lives in final fields on the enum (or in constant-specific class bodies). The coverage proof is real but the variants cannot carry different record shapes, and adding an operation means editing the enum or switching over it in one more place; use this when the alternatives share one payload schema, and migrate to sealed interfaces plus records once cases diverge in shape.
pitfalls: A default arm is mandatory again the moment the switch is written as a statement, and it silently disables the check for constants added later.
Enum constants can only share a single payload schema (final fields), so divergent variant data forces nullable fields, side maps or a move to sealed records.

Since Java 21 a switch expression over an enum that lacks the constant added after compilation throws MatchException (previously IncompatibleClassChangeError), so consumers must be rebuilt with the enum.
